html:
SMTO-CFG-0059 — SMTO doesn't recognize the Gateway name it was asked to use

GUID: 92bd9c40-1dd8-4442-af8d-ed5511643fc9
Slug: config-node-is-not-available-available-nodes
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to use a Gateway — the helper program it uses to run commands on a computer — by a name that isn't in its list of Gateway names, so it didn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel. If it shows the name SMTO was asked for and a list after Available nodes, compare the two. This shows whether the name is misspelled or simply missing from SMTO's list.
  2. Under the message box, select the Target button, choose a Gateway under Execution target, and send your message again. The Gateways offered there are ones SMTO already knows.
  3. If the name should exist, ask the person who installed SMTO to add it to AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES, or correct AOR_DEFAULT_NODE, where SMTO is started, then restart SMTO. SMTO matches Gateway names exactly, including spelling and capital letters.

What success looks like

  • Your message runs on the Gateway you chose, and that Gateway shows as connected in Settings › Setup › Gateways.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't give another computer's Gateway this name; commands meant for one computer would run on the other.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings.resolve_node rejected the requested or default node because the name is not in available_nodes (AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES, gateway_endpoints keys and default_node).

What this means

  • The requested/default node name is absent from available_nodes at resolution. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The requested/default node name is absent from available_nodes at resolution.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact requested node with the current configured names; the name check does not establish network reachability.

How to fix it

  • Compare the requested name with the Available nodes list in the message, then add the node to AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES or gateway_endpoints, or correct AOR_DEFAULT_NODE (exact, case-sensitive), and restart the Server. With several nodes and no default, the runtime engine bridge and terminal lookup ask for 'localhost', fail this check and fall back (no legacy Gateway URL, or http://127.0.0.1:8787 for the terminal), so set AOR_DEFAULT_NODE explicitly. Name check only; Gateway readiness is verified separately.
  • Configure an existing enabled Gateway node and select it explicitly or as the intended default. Keep endpoint names and node identities consistent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended configured node resolves and separate Gateway admission verifies its readiness.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
